cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The baseline RED probe reached legacy presentation construction without a C0 owner or projection admission.
impact: P0-A allowed legacy presentation IO before fail-closed admission.
lesson: Gate every legacy presentation read before summary, template, or filesystem access.

cause: The GREEN probe now returns typed unavailable before any legacy presentation, template, fact, or filesystem seam.
impact: P0-A missing-admission and forged-input paths are fail closed before presentation IO while the admitted owner path remains available.
lesson: Gate every legacy presentation read before summary, template, or filesystem access.

cause: The baseline HTTP evidence and export probes observed artifact index or hash work before server owner admission.
impact: P0-B allowed artifact reads or hashing before proof, receipt, and canonical owner admission.
lesson: Admit the real server owner before opening an artifact index or hashing any export input.

cause: The GREEN order probes observe server owner admission before artifact index access, path resolution, or hashing for evidence and export.
impact: P0-B evidence and export entrances now fail closed before artifact IO and preserve the admitted owner path.
lesson: Admit the real server owner before opening an artifact index or hashing any export input.

cause: The baseline clone probe copied valid projection and writer fields, then reached canonical report IO because field markers were the only admission proof.
impact: P0-C object.__new__ clones could impersonate server-issued projections or document writers before facts or writer IO.
lesson: Require an exact server-issued identity registry in every projection and writer consumer.

cause: The GREEN clone probe rejects copied and serialized projection or writer objects before canonical facts, template, or filesystem seams; real owner-issued objects remain usable.
impact: P0-C consumers and writers now require exact object identity retained by the server issuer registry.
lesson: Require an exact server-issued identity registry in every projection and writer consumer.

cause: The baseline ReportStage probe found no owner/projection adapter and the normal stage had no typed admission path for legacy rendering.
impact: P1-D normal report rendering could fail or fall back without adapting the server-owned C0 report receipt.
lesson: Adapt the exact stage-owned report admission and fail typed unavailable when it is absent.

cause: The GREEN ReportStage probe adapts the exact owner/projection from stage context and returns no admission for missing or forged inputs.
impact: P1-D now preserves the legal owner path and fails typed unavailable without restoring a raw summary fallback.
lesson: Adapt the exact stage-owned report admission and fail typed unavailable when it is absent.

cause: The default restricted runner could not bind the Unix socket used by the real owner fixture; the same probes were rerun on a socket-capable host.
impact: The direct HTTP, export, and exact-owner probes require a socket-capable host for valid evidence.
lesson: Record restricted-host socket failures separately and rerun authority probes on the supported host.

cause: The rem6 direct owner/order/clone/stage probes, focused Evidence/Report suite, formal event tests, compileall, and diff check all passed.
impact: The P0-A, P0-B, P0-C, and P1-D implementation boundary is verified for the scoped host-capable test surface.
lesson: Keep direct admission order and exact-identity probes alongside the focused report suite before closeout.

cause: Remediation-6 implementation, adversarial RED/GREEN probes, scoped verification gate, and formal event verification are complete.
impact: The scoped P0-A, P0-B, P0-C, and P1-D Evidence/Report boundary is handed off with external acceptance limits retained.
lesson: Complete a scoped line only after direct boundary probes, focused verification, and formal integrity are recorded.
